objectives.statement: Identify C# as a statically typed language in which every variable and expression has a type.
Distinguish value types from reference types in the C# type system.
objectives.citation: C# type system: value types and reference types

objectives.statement: Explain how a local variable declared with var receives a compile-time inferred type.
Identify the role of generic type parameters in writing reusable strongly typed code.
Distinguish if, else and switch as C# selection statements.
Explain how a C# method declaration specifies a return type, name and parameter list.
Explain that a class defines a type and objects are instances created from that type.
Distinguish generic classes and methods from code specialized for only one data type.
Identify while, do and for as iteration statements and distinguish their control points.
Distinguish parameters passed by value from ref and out parameter passing modes.
Explain inheritance as a mechanism by which a derived class reuses and extends a base class.
Explain generic type safety and the role of type parameters in avoiding casts.
Identify break and continue as statements that alter loop execution.
Explain how try, catch and finally structure exception handling.
Distinguish encapsulation through access modifiers such as public and private.
Identify LINQ as a set of technologies for querying data using language-integrated query operators.
Explain pattern matching as a way to test an expression against a pattern and optionally extract information.
Explain how throw transfers control by raising an exception and how exception filters can constrain catches.
Distinguish virtual, override and abstract members in polymorphic class hierarchies.
Explain generic constraints as restrictions on the type arguments that may be supplied.
